panels.title: Status — is the node up, ready and holding its data
Ready — overall (HealthNotReady, CRITICAL)
panels.description: The node's own readiness self-report, sampled from the same body /health/ready serves. The per-subsystem breakdown is the state timeline under Serving.

panels.title: Synthetic probes (SyntheticProbeDown, CRITICAL)
panels.description: blackbox-exporter probes of /health/ready, /health/live and /fairdp from outside the process — one tile per target, latest sample only. Its `instance` is the probed URL, so it is not filtered by the Node variable.

panels.title: Keyless-degraded (KeylessDegraded, CRITICAL)
panels.description: 1 when [vault] is configured but was unreachable at startup: encrypted-package ingest is skipped and readiness stays 503. Latched — a restart with Vault reachable clears it.

panels.title: At-rest master key (PmeMasterKeyMismatch, CRITICAL)
panels.description: 1 when the configured Transit master key can no longer unwrap a DEK this node wrote (replaced key or reset secrets backend): PME parquet at rest is undecryptable and the node reports ready:false. Latched. A restart alone changes nothing — restore or roll the key first (operating.md §10). Absent unless [vault].transit_key is set.

panels.title: Build
panels.description: Crate version and the git commit the binary was built from (`unknown` for a plain from-source build; see operating.md §18).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Process uptime. Neutral by design: there is no threshold a running process can fail.

panels.title: Datasets by state (DatasetsInError)
panels.description: Datasets per lifecycle state. `error` includes datasets not in the cache (a failed ingest leaves no store); `processing` is never in the cache by design, so it reads 0 here — watch ingest in-flight instead.

panels.title: Datasets at rest, by form (DatasetsPlaintextAtRest, DatasetsIndeterminateAtRest)
panels.description: Dataset stores by on-disk form. Emitted only when PME ([vault].transit_key) is configured — on a node that never enabled it every store is plaintext by design and the panel is empty. `indeterminate` = no readable parquet, not known to be encrypted.

panels.title: Data volume free (LowDisk, CRITICAL)
panels.description: Free bytes on data_dir. The yellow step is the shipped LowDisk margin (a placeholder far below peak ingest scratch — operating.md §7); scripts/check-dashboard-metrics.py keeps it equal to the rule's threshold.

panels.title: Store scrub (StoreScrubFailed, StoreScrubStale)
panels.description: Left: datasets that failed the last detached store-readability sweep (on-disk corruption). Right: how long ago a sweep last completed — a 0 on the left means nothing if the sweep never runs.

panels.title: Serving — HTTP, Beacon, FDP (rate, errors, latency)
Request rate by plane / status class
panels.description: Every completed request on both listeners, by status class: the public plane (Beacon + FDP + informational routes) and the management plane (probes, scrapes, the oracle).

panels.title: Error ratio — public plane (5xx / 4xx)
panels.description: Share of public-plane responses that were server errors (5xx) or client errors (4xx — Beacon guardrails such as a missing assemblyId land here). Empty while there is no traffic.

panels.title: Request latency p50 / p95 / p99 by plane
panels.description: Whole-node request latency. The histogram's lowest buckets are 0.25 ms and 1 ms, so a sub-millisecond typical request reads as such rather than as an interpolated 2.5 ms.

panels.title: Beacon request rate by entry type / status (BeaconServingErrors)
panels.description: Transport-level Beacon volume per entry type. BeaconServingErrors pages on a sustained 5xx ratio of this series.

panels.title: Beacon latency p50 / p95 by entry type
Beacon queries: hit / miss and rejected by code
panels.description: Handler-level semantics: answered queries by hit/miss (exists) at the granted disclosure level, and queries rejected before or within the scan by HTTP code (400 malformed or too broad, 413 too broad, 500 in-scan failure) — the split the transport status class cannot give.

panels.title: FDP request rate by resource type / status (FdpServingErrors, CRITICAL)
panels.description: FAIR Data Point volume by resource kind. FdpServingErrors pages on a sustained 5xx ratio. Empty on a node without [fairdp].

panels.title: Requests rejected by a resilience layer, by reason (HttpRequestsRejected)
panels.description: Load-shed 503 / timeout 408 / body 413 / URI 414 / internal 500 — rejections the per-route counters never see.

panels.title: HTTP in-flight vs capacity (HttpInflightSaturated)
panels.description: Public-plane requests being served against the configured max_concurrent_requests. The alert fires above 80% for 10 minutes; load-shed 503s start at the line.

panels.title: Connections dropped at accept, by plane (HttpConnectionsRejected)
panels.description: The plane's connection cap was full, so the connection never became a request. On the management plane this sits below the health-probe exemption and starves the kubelet.

panels.title: Beacon scans on the blocking pool vs query capacity (IngestPoolStarvedByQueries)
panels.description: Per-dataset parquet scans currently on tokio's shared blocking pool (including scans detached by a request timeout) against the query fan-out cap. Sustained values at 2× the cap starve ingest, which shares the pool.

panels.title: Readiness by subsystem (HealthNotReady, CRITICAL)
panels.description: One row per subsystem, red while not ready. `overall` is the AND of the configured subsystems; a not-configured subsystem reports ready. Sampled from the same body /health/ready serves, so the two cannot disagree.

panels.title: Queue / in-flight vs worker capacity (WedgedIngestPool, IngestPoolSaturated)
panels.description: Jobs waiting, jobs being processed, and the node-wide ingest_concurrency they share across the inbox and every bucket. Queued > 0 with in-flight == 0 for 5 minutes is the wedge signal; in-flight at capacity for 10 minutes is saturation.

panels.title: Ingest outcomes per hour (IngestTimeout, IngestRetryChurn)
panels.description: Completed ingest jobs per outcome class over the trailing hour. Ingests are rare events (one per package), so an hourly count reads better than a per-second rate.

panels.title: Ingest duration — hourly mean and p90
panels.description: Wall-clock ingest time over a one-hour window. A 5-minute rate over one-per-package events yields a blip and then NaN; the hourly window keeps a value on screen between packages.

panels.title: Last-progress age while work is queued
panels.description: Seconds since the pool last picked up or finished a job, shown only while something is queued — on an idle node the age grows without meaning, so it is blanked. A rising line here is the visual form of WedgedIngestPool; read it with the queue panel.

panels.title: Oldest in-flight ingest age (DatasetStuckProcessing)
panels.description: Seconds the longest-held in-flight ingest marker (queued or being processed) has been held; 0 when nothing is in flight. Past 30 minutes this is DatasetStuckProcessing: one ingest that never finished. A steady stream of short ingests cannot raise it, which a window over the in-flight count cannot distinguish.

panels.title: Sources in transient-failure backoff (IngestSourceBackoff)
panels.description: Distinct sources currently in a backoff window after transient failures — a persistently failing backend (Vault, S3) keeps a source here; cleared on its first successful ingest.

panels.title: Split-package block merges per hour (Beacon scan cost)
panels.description: Blocks a Beacon scan had to buffer and sort whole because several source VCFs cover the same positions (a per-population split package). Peak memory for that arm is bounded by neither granularity nor limit; the remedy is how the provider builds the package (operating.md §22).

panels.title: Writer-policy and provenance events per hour (WriterKeyNotAllowed, ProvenanceRecoveryFailed)
panels.description: Packages from a writer key not on the channel's allow-list (warn: published; enforce: quarantined) and published packages with no recoverable writer key. reason=plaintext is expected on every inbox staging drop; recovery_failed is the anomalous one.

panels.title: Decrypt failures / background panics per hour (DecryptFailures, BackgroundPanics)
Manifest reloads skipped / FDP serialization failures per hour (ManifestReloadSkipped, FdpSerializationFailures)
panels.description: A published dataset dropped from serving on a cache reload because its manifest.json was unreadable; and the FDP's empty-output 500 branch.

panels.title: S3 last successful poll — age per channel (S3PollerWedged)
panels.description: Seconds since each bucket's last successful listing. Seeded to boot time, so a bucket that never polls successfully ages from the start.

panels.title: Inbox last successful scan — age (InboxScanWedged)
panels.description: Seconds since the inbox was last scanned successfully. Absent on a node without an inbox.

panels.title: Inbox backlog: quarantined / keyless packages (InboxQuarantineBacklog, InboxKeylessPackages)
panels.description: Standing backlogs an operator must clear: permanently-rejected packages parked in inbox/.rejected, and encrypted packages this node holds no crypt4gh identity for (they wait silently until a keyed run).

panels.title: S3 status writeback (StatusWritebackDisabled)
panels.description: Per bucket: writeback of _status/{id}.json is disabled after an AccessDenied and stays disabled until the grant is fixed. Seeded 0 per configured bucket, so a healthy bucket shows `enabled` rather than nothing.

panels.title: S3 poll / download errors per 15 min, per channel (S3PollErrors, S3DownloadErrors)
panels.description: Listing-leg failures and fetch-leg failures separately: a bucket that lists fine but whose packages never download shows healthy poll age with download errors here.

panels.title: S3 reconcile: mass removal skipped / deleted-sidecar ignored per hour (MassRemovalSkipped, DeletedSidecarIgnored)
panels.description: Fail-safe events: the reconcile refused a mass eviction because the listing collapsed (served data retained — check the endpoint), and a `deleted` .state.json was ignored because on S3 deletion means removing the object.

panels.title: Inbox: watcher restarts / quarantine evictions per hour (InboxWatcherFlapping)
S3 package downloads per hour
panels.description: Successful package fetches in the trailing hour — the pre-ingest network leg that runs before the ingest timer starts.

panels.title: Metadata-overlay apply failures per hour, by channel / reason (OverlayApplyFailing)
panels.description: A broken governance overlay keeps serving last-good metadata silently; this is the only signal. Covers the inbox, every bucket, and the node-local override feed.

panels.title: Visibility-sidecar rejections per hour, by channel / reason (StateSidecarRejected)
panels.description: A {id}.state.json that could not be read: the dataset failed safe to hidden — a live dataset dropped off the public plane because someone's write was truncated.

panels.title: Token lease at last login (VaultTokenLeaseTooShort, CRITICAL)
panels.description: The full lease the token was issued with, re-stamped on every login/renew. A step value, never a countdown. 0 means a static or agent-managed token (no lease to report) — neutral, not a fault. Red only when a lease was issued shorter than the 10-minute margin.

panels.title: Token file age (VaultTokenFileStale, CRITICAL)

defaults.noValue: no sample: token_file unset, or unreadable since boot

panels.description: now − mtime of [vault].token_file. Under an agent sidecar the node never renews, so a climbing age is the only evidence the agent died. Absent unless token_file is configured — and absent, not stale, when the file has been unreadable since boot (the gauge is written only on a successful stat; VaultTokenFileUnreadable counts the failures). A file that vanishes after boot freezes this at its last value; that alert, not this tile, is the signal.

panels.title: Token file reloads / read errors (24 h) (VaultTokenFileUnreadable, CRITICAL)
panels.description: Successful re-reads of the token file (one per detected rotation) and failed reads (missing, empty, unreadable). Absent unless token_file is configured.

panels.title: Vault call errors (15 min, by operation) (VaultCallErrors)
panels.description: KV/Transit failures on the data path (PME key fetch, crypt4gh unwrap) — a Vault dependency fault, distinct from the token lifecycle.

panels.title: Re-authentication outcomes and renewal failures per hour (VaultRenewalFailing, CRITICAL)
panels.description: The alert keys on re-auth outcome=failed: a renewal failed AND the fallback re-login failed, so the credential is unusable. outcome=recovered is the routine token_max_ttl rollover. Renewal failures alone rise once per max TTL on a healthy node — context, never a page.

panels.title: Vault call latency p90 by operation
Vault call errors per 15 min by operation (VaultCallErrors)
Datasets suppressed, by mode
panels.description: Datasets withheld by an operator suppression override: hide = reversible; remove = marked for eviction. Inventory, not a fault — the exact ids come from `dataset list --suppressed`.

panels.title: Channel suppressed (ChannelSuppressed)
panels.description: A whole channel (bucket or inbox) under an operator suppression override: every dataset withheld, ingest paused.

panels.title: Orphaned catalog / S3 channel (CatalogOrphaned, S3ChannelOrphaned)
panels.description: Catalog: visible datasets declare a [catalogs] entry that was removed — still served, but unreachable by crawling the FDP. Channel: datasets remain from a [[s3.buckets]] entry that was removed — withheld, nothing polls them. Channel orphans appear only when one exists (the label cannot be seeded).

panels.title: S3 keyspace mismatch (S3KeyspaceMismatch)
panels.description: The channel's configured endpoint/bucket/prefix is not the keyspace its datasets were ingested from, so removal processing is refused (serving and additions continue).

panels.title: Override store (OverrideStoreAbsent, SuppressionStoreDegraded)
panels.description: Left: 1 when the whole override-store root is gone while require_override_store is set — the node serves its last in-memory set and no new hide/correct can take effect. Right: suppression files that failed to parse on the last load (each fail-closed to hide).

panels.title: Config reloads failed (24 h) (ConfigReloadFailed)
panels.description: SIGHUP reloads that failed validation and were discarded — the node kept its previous [catalogs] and writer allow-list. The paired WARN log names the reason.

panels.title: Disk sample (DiskSampleFailed)
panels.description: 1 when statvfs on data_dir is failing: the free-bytes gauge is then stale and LowDisk cannot fire. Check that the volume is still mounted and readable.

panels.title: Resident memory (RSS)
panels.description: node_exporter-independent memory signal for the long-lived streaming process.

panels.title: Open file descriptors
panels.description: Catches an fd leak before EMFILE.

panels.title: CPU cores in use
panels.description: Rate of cumulative CPU seconds (user + system): 1.0 = one core pinned. The gauge carries fractional seconds, so a lightly loaded node reads a small non-zero value rather than 0.

panels.title: Node logs (service=gdi-node-standalone)
panels.description: The node's own structured logs, shipped by Alloy to Loki. Selected on `service` (the Compose service name), not on `job` and not on `container`. `job` is docker-logs on every container, so it does not discriminate. `container` is `<project>-<service>-<n>` — e.g. gdi-node-standalone-gdi-node-standalone-1 — so it changes with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME. An empty panel here means the Alloy -> Loki pipeline is broken, not that the node is quiet; that is the point of showing it next to the metrics. Use Explore for other containers, ad-hoc LogQL, and the Tempo trace-id derived field.

list.name: instance
list.label: Node
list.description: Which node's series to show. Every panel filters on it; the synthetic-probe tile does not (its instance is the probed URL).
